questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding dipole moments and molecular symmetry:

(a) Boron trifluoride ($\text{BF}_3$) has a net dipole moment of zero ($\mu = 0$), whereas nitrogen trifluoride ($\text{NF}_3$) has a permanent dipole moment ($\mu = 0.24\text{ D}$).
(b) The experimental dipole moment of chloromethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$, $1.86\text{ D}$) is higher than that of fluoromethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{F}$, $1.60\text{ D}$), because the much longer $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bond distance overcompensates for the smaller charge difference ($\mu = q \times d$).
(c) Carbon tetrachloride ($\text{CCl}_4$) and chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) both have a net dipole moment of zero due to tetrahedral symmetry.
(d) 1,4-Dichlorobenzene possesses a net dipole moment of zero ($\mu = 0$), whereas 1,4-dihydroxybenzene (hydroquinone) can possess a non-zero dipole moment due to non-collinear orientation of bent $\text{C}-\text{O}-\text{H}$ groups.

Which of the above statements are correct?
options: A) (a), (b), and (d) only
B) (a) and (b) only
C) (b), (c), and (d) only
D) (a), (c), and (d) only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate statement (a): $\text{BF}_3$ is symmetrical trigonal planar with bond dipoles canceling completely ($\mu = 0$). $\text{NF}_3$ is trigonal pyramidal with an uncancelled dipole moment ($\mu = 0.24\text{ D}$). Statement (a) is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate statement (b): Dipole moment is the product of charge and distance ($\mu = q \times d$). Although the $\text{C}-\text{F}$ bond has higher partial charges, the $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bond length ($178\text{ pm}$) is significantly longer than the $\text{C}-\text{F}$ bond length ($139\text{ pm}$). The greater distance dominates, resulting in $\mu(\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}) = 1.86\text{ D} > \mu(\text{CH}_3\text{F}) = 1.60\text{ D}$ (a classic NCERT point). Statement (b) is correct.
Step 3: Evaluate statement (c): In $\text{CCl}_4$, all four $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ dipoles cancel symmetrically ($\mu = 0$). In $\text{CHCl}_3$, the three $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ dipoles and one $\text{C}-\text{H}$ dipole are not identical, resulting in an uncancelled dipole moment of $\mu = 1.04\text{ D}$. Statement (c) is incorrect.
Step 4: Evaluate statement (d): In 1,4-dichlorobenzene, the two $\text{C}-\text{Cl}$ bonds are collinear along the aromatic axis at $180^\circ$ ($\mu = 0$). In hydroquinone, the $\text{C}-\text{O}-\text{H}$ angle is approximately $109^\circ$ (bent); rotation around the $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bond allows conformations where the two $\text{O}-\text{H}$ dipoles do not cancel, giving a net dipole moment ($\mu \ne 0$). Statement (d) is correct.
Step 5: Hence, statements (a), (b), and (d) only are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match the types of atomic orbital combinations in List I (taking the $z$-axis as the internuclear axis) with the nature of the resulting overlap or bond in List II:

List I:
A. Positive lobe of $s$ + positive lobe of $s$ along $z$-axis
B. Positive lobe of $p_z$ + positive lobe of $p_z$ along $z$-axis
C. Positive lobe of $p_x$ + positive lobe of $p_x$ perpendicular to $z$-axis
D. Positive lobe of $s$ approaching a $p_x$ orbital along the $z$-axis

List II:
I. Coaxial $\sigma$ bond formed by directional $p$-orbital overlap
II. Lateral $\pi$ bond with a nodal plane containing the internuclear axis
III. Zero overlap resulting in no bond formation
IV. Spherically symmetrical coaxial $\sigma$ bond

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-I, B-IV, C-II, D-III
B) A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
C) A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III
D) A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze each orbital combination according to Valence Bond Theory:
- A ($s + s$ along $z$-axis): Axial overlap of non-directional $s$-orbitals creates a cylindrically symmetrical $\sigma$ bond with electron density concentrated symmetrically between the nuclei (A matches IV).
- B ($p_z + p_z$ along $z$-axis): End-to-end head-on overlap of directional $p_z$ lobes along the internuclear axis forms a strong coaxial $\sigma$ bond (B matches I).
- C ($p_x + p_x$ perpendicular to $z$-axis): Sideways parallel overlap of $p_x$ lobes above and below the internuclear axis produces a lateral $\pi$ bond with the internuclear $z$-axis lying in the nodal plane (C matches II).
- D ($s + p_x$ along $z$-axis): The spherical $s$-orbital overlaps equally with the positive lobe and negative lobe of the perpendicular $p_x$-orbital. Positive and negative overlap integrals cancel out exactly, giving net zero overlap and no chemical bond (D matches III).
Step 2: Correct matching order: A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III, which corresponds to option C.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding isoelectronic and isostructural relationships among polyatomic chemical species:

(a) The carbonate ion ($\text{CO}_3^{2-}$) and nitrate ion ($\text{NO}_3^-$) are isoelectronic with 24 valence electrons and are isostructural with trigonal planar geometry ($sp^2$ hybridization).
(b) The chlorate ion ($\text{ClO}_3^-$) and sulfite ion ($\text{SO}_3^{2-}$) are isoelectronic with 26 valence electrons and are isostructural with trigonal pyramidal geometry ($sp^3$ hybridization).
(c) Xenon difluoride ($\text{XeF}_2$) and carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) are isostructural because both are linear molecules with central atoms possessing $sp$ hybridization.
(d) The tetrafluoroborate ion ($\text{BF}_4^-$) and ammonium ion ($\text{NH}_4^+$) are isostructural with regular tetrahedral geometry ($sp^3$ hybridization).

Which of the above statements are correct?
options: A) (a) and (b) only
B) (a), (b), and (d) only
C) (b), (c), and (d) only
D) (a), (c), and (d) only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate statement (a): Valence electrons: $\text{CO}_3^{2-} = 4 + 3(6) + 2 = 24$; $\text{NO}_3^- = 5 + 3(6) + 1 = 24$. Both central atoms have steric number 3 (3 $\sigma$ bonds, 0 lone pairs), yielding $sp^2$ trigonal planar geometry. Statement (a) is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate statement (b): Valence electrons: $\text{ClO}_3^- = 7 + 3(6) + 1 = 26$; $\text{SO}_3^{2-} = 6 + 3(6) + 2 = 26$. Both have steric number 4 (3 $\sigma$ bonds, 1 lone pair), yielding $sp^3$ trigonal pyramidal geometry. Statement (b) is correct.
Step 3: Evaluate statement (c): Although both molecules are linear in shape, $\text{CO}_2$ has $sp$ hybridization (2 bond pairs, 0 lone pairs), whereas $\text{XeF}_2$ has $sp^3d$ hybridization (2 bond pairs, 3 lone pairs in equatorial positions). They do not share the same hybridization. Statement (c) is incorrect.
Step 4: Evaluate statement (d): In $\text{BF}_4^-$, boron has steric number 4 (4 bond pairs, 0 lone pairs, $sp^3$, tetrahedral). In $\text{NH}_4^+$, nitrogen has steric number 4 (4 bond pairs, 0 lone pairs, $sp^3$, tetrahedral). Both are isostructural. Statement (d) is correct.
Step 5: Thus, statements (a), (b), and (d) only are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match the dioxygen species in List I with their corresponding bond order and magnetic nature in List II according to Molecular Orbital Theory:

List I:
A. $\text{O}_2^+$
B. $\text{O}_2^-$
C. $\text{O}_2^{2-}$
D. $\text{O}_2$

List II:
I. $\text{Bond Order} = 1.0$, Diamagnetic
II. $\text{Bond Order} = 1.5$, Paramagnetic (1 unpaired electron)
III. $\text{Bond Order} = 2.0$, Paramagnetic (2 unpaired electrons)
IV. $\text{Bond Order} = 2.5$, Paramagnetic (1 unpaired electron)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
B) A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
C) A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
D) A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Write MO configuration and calculate parameters for each species:
- A ($\text{O}_2^+$): 15 electrons. Configuration ends with $(\pi^* 2p_x^1 = \pi^* 2p_y^0)$. Bond order $= \frac{1}{2}(10 - 5) = 2.5$; has 1 unpaired electron, paramagnetic (A matches IV).
- B ($\text{O}_2^-$): 17 electrons. Configuration ends with $(\pi^* 2p_x^2 = \pi^* 2p_y^1)$. Bond order $= \frac{1}{2}(10 - 7) = 1.5$; has 1 unpaired electron, paramagnetic (B matches II).
- C ($\text{O}_2^{2-}$): 18 electrons. Configuration ends with $(\pi^* 2p_x^2 = \pi^* 2p_y^2)$. Bond order $= \frac{1}{2}(10 - 8) = 1.0$; zero unpaired electrons, diamagnetic (C matches I).
- D ($\text{O}_2$): 16 electrons. Configuration ends with $(\pi^* 2p_x^1 = \pi^* 2p_y^1)$. Bond order $= \frac{1}{2}(10 - 6) = 2.0$; has 2 unpaired electrons, paramagnetic (D matches III).
Step 2: Correct matching order: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III, which corresponds to option D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding resonance stabilization and bond parameters in organic and inorganic molecules:

(a) In the acetate ion ($\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^-$), both carbon-oxygen bonds are of identical length and have an equal fractional bond order of $1.5$.
(b) In benzene ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$), all six carbon-carbon bonds have an identical experimental length of $139\text{ pm}$, lying intermediate between a pure single bond ($154\text{ pm}$) and a pure double bond ($134\text{ pm}$).
(c) The resonance energy of a molecule is rigorously defined as the energy difference between the least stable canonical contributing structure and the resonance hybrid.
(d) In the nitrate ion ($\text{NO}_3^-$), all three nitrogen-oxygen bonds are completely equivalent in length with a calculated bond order of $1.33$.

Which of the above statements are correct?
options: A) (a) and (b) only
B) (a), (c), and (d) only
C) (a), (b), and (d) only
D) (b), (c), and (d) only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate statement (a): In the acetate anion, resonance delocalizes the negative charge equally over both oxygen atoms, making both $\text{C}-\text{O}$ bonds equivalent with bond order $\frac{1 + 2}{2} = 1.5$. Statement (a) is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate statement (b): The resonance hybrid of benzene delocalizes $6$ $\pi$ electrons evenly over the ring, resulting in six equal $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bonds of $139\text{ pm}$, intermediate between $154\text{ pm}$ ($	ext{C}-	ext{C}$) and $134\text{ pm}$ ($	ext{C}=	ext{C}$). Statement (b) is correct.
Step 3: Evaluate statement (c): By definition, resonance energy is the difference between the energy of the resonance hybrid and the energy of the *most stable* (lowest energy) canonical structure, NOT the least stable. Statement (c) is incorrect.
Step 4: Evaluate statement (d): In $\text{NO}_3^-$, three equivalent resonance structures distribute one double bond and two single bonds over three $\text{N}-\text{O}$ positions, yielding an average bond order of $\frac{4}{3} = 1.33$ and strictly identical bond lengths. Statement (d) is correct.
Step 5: Hence, statements (a), (b), and (d) only are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match the molecules in List I with the complete set of ideal bond angles present within their geometric frameworks in List II:

List I:
A. $\text{SF}_6$
B. $\text{PCl}_5$
C. $\text{BF}_3$
D. $\text{CH}_4$

List II:
I. Only $120^\circ$
II. Only $109^\circ 28'$
III. Both $90^\circ$ and $120^\circ$ (and $180^\circ$ between axial bonds)
IV. Both $90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
B) A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
C) A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II
D) A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Determine the bond angles for each molecule based on regular geometries:
- A ($\text{SF}_6$): Regular octahedral geometry ($sp^3d^2$). All adjacent bonds lie at $90^\circ$ to each other, and opposite axial bonds lie at $180^\circ$. A matches IV.
- B ($\text{PCl}_5$): Regular trigonal bipyramidal geometry ($sp^3d$). Equatorial-equatorial angle is $120^\circ$, axial-equatorial angle is $90^\circ$, and axial-axial angle is $180^\circ$. B matches III.
- C ($\text{BF}_3$): Regular trigonal planar geometry ($sp^2$). All three $\text{F}-\text{B}-\text{F}$ bond angles are strictly $120^\circ$. C matches I.
- D ($\text{CH}_4$): Regular tetrahedral geometry ($sp^3$). All four $\text{H}-\text{C}-\text{H}$ bond angles are strictly $109^\circ 28'$ ($109.5^\circ$). D matches II.
Step 2: Correct matching order: A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II, which corresponds to option A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding hydrogen bonding and anomalous physical phenomena:

(a) The typical bond energy of a hydrogen bond ranges from $10$ to $40\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, which is significantly weaker than a normal covalent bond ($200-400\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) but substantially stronger than van der Waals dispersion forces.
(b) In non-polar solvents and in the vapor phase, acetic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) exists predominantly as a stable cyclic dimer with an apparent molecular mass of 120 due to two intermolecular hydrogen bonds.
(c) The density of water increases as it is warmed from $0^\circ\text{C}$ to $4^\circ\text{C}$ because thermal kinetic expansion overrides the breakdown of the hydrogen-bonded cage structure.
(d) Salicylaldehyde is steam volatile and has a lower boiling point than its *para*-isomer because it forms an intramolecular hydrogen bond between its phenolic $-\text{OH}$ and carbonyl oxygen.

Which of the above statements are correct?
options: A) (a) and (b) only
B) (b), (c), and (d) only
C) (a), (c), and (d) only
D) (a), (b), and (d) only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate statement (a): Covalent bonds have energies around $200-450\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, van der Waals forces are $< 8\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, and hydrogen bonds have intermediate energies of $10-40\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ (or up to $100\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ in $[	ext{F}-	ext{H}\cdots\text{F}]^-$). Statement (a) is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate statement (b): In benzene and in the vapor phase, two molecules of acetic acid join head-to-tail by two intermolecular hydrogen bonds forming an eight-membered ring dimer with formula $(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH})_2$ and molecular weight $120$. Statement (b) is correct.
Step 3: Evaluate statement (c): Between $0^\circ\text{C}$ and $4^\circ\text{C}$, the collapse of the open tetrahedral cage structure upon melting causes water molecules to pack more closely into the cavities. This contraction *dominates over* normal thermal expansion, causing density to increase to a maximum at $4^\circ\text{C}$. Statement (c) falsely asserts that thermal expansion overrides cage collapse. Statement (c) is incorrect.
Step 4: Evaluate statement (d): In salicylaldehyde, the adjacent $-\text{OH}$ and $-\text{CHO}$ groups form an intramolecular six-membered chelate ring via H-bonding, preventing intermolecular association and rendering it steam volatile with a lower boiling point. Statement (d) is correct.
Step 5: Therefore, statements (a), (b), and (d) only are correct.
